title: `enum`: more than a constant, a type with behaviour

videos.script: A library sorts its books into genres. Fiction, history, science, poetry. Four values and no others. {{basics}} You could write them as four strings, or four numbers, and a typo would sail through the compiler. An enum makes them a type. The compiler then knows every value there is, and a switch that forgets one does not compile. {{behaviour}} An enum is also a class. Each constant can carry fields, a constructor sets them, and methods use them. One constant can even behave differently from the rest. {{collections}} Then two collections built for enums, a set and a map, faster and smaller than the general ones. {{ordinal}} Last, a warning with a demonstration. Every constant has a position number, and storing that number is a mistake. Somebody adds a genre at the top, and every saved book moves to the wrong shelf. Nothing fails. By the end you can model a fixed set of values as a type, and store it safely.
